recipe.title: Review canary changes, draining, and return to service
recipe.scenario: A release owner is deciding whether to increase a canary share, hold it, recommend draining a target, or restore a recovered target. Compare observed performance with operator-approved limits and check the capacity of the proposed fallback. No routing, connection, or deployment change is performed.

field.name: change-window-utc
field.description: UTC review period, snapshot timestamp, and current configuration revision. Missing revision, incomplete coverage, future-dated samples, or inconsistent clocks require operator review.

field.name: current-stage
field.description: Current operator-reported stage: observing-canary, draining, or validating-recovery. Use the reported state, not the desired next state, when checking constraints.

field.name: candidate-traffic-steps
field.description: Allowed progression steps for new traffic expressed in basis points (100 basis points equal one percentage point). Keep existing flows and DNS caches separate from the proposed new-traffic share.

field.name: health-and-slo-observations
field.description: Rows of stable and canary cohort IDs, sample time, status, request count, error rate, and latency percentile with units. Missing or sparse observations do not establish readiness; compare the cohorts over the approved window.

field.name: guardrail-limits
field.description: Operator-approved limits for health freshness, minimum sample count, maximum error rate and latency, minimum reserve on fallback, and consecutive healthy observation windows before failback.

field.name: fallback-capacity
field.description: Rows of eligible fallback targets, existing load, remaining safe capacity, and observation timestamp. Do not treat a rollback or drain as viable if remaining targets cannot absorb the proposed new traffic.

field.name: in-flight-work
field.description: Rows of target, active connections or streams, expected drain window and freshness. Draining can stop new placement without ending current work; unknown connection counts or overdue sessions need an operator decision.

field.name: advisory-action
field.description: Return hold, recommend-next-step, recommend-drain, or recommend-failback. A known regression may justify proposing drain if fallback fits. Without current evidence or capacity, return hold with escalation rather than treating a missing signal as success.

field.name: guardrail-evidence
field.description: Expected threshold, observed value and unit, sample time, and pass/fail/unknown for each gate. Include recent stable observation windows before recommending failback; healthy probes alone do not establish acceptable request performance.

field.name: operator-handoff
field.description: List remaining conflicts, the smallest suggested traffic change, what to confirm about active sessions, and what would require reverting. Proposal only; any platform or production change is outside this recipe.
